desc:
Find the length of the longest string t that satisfies all three conditions:

  • t is a non-empty proper prefix of s;
  • t is also a suffix of s;
  • t occurs a third time inside s, starting at some index i with 0 < i < n - |t| (so this occurrence is neither the prefix nor the suffix; it may overlap them).

Return |t|, or 0 if no such string exists.

Example: for s = "abcabcab" the border "abcab" has no third copy, but the border "ab" also occurs at index 3, so the answer is 2. For s = "aaaa" the answer is 2: the string "aa" is a prefix, a suffix, and also occurs at index 1.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters
hints: First list the candidates: only borders of s can be t. Which of them have a third occurrence?
A prefix of length L occurs ending at index j (with j ≤ n-2) as soon as pi[j] ≥ L. So all you need is M = max(pi[0..n-2]).
Walk the border chain pi[n-1], pi[pi[n-1]-1], ... from the longest to the shortest and return the first value that is at most M; if the chain ends, return 0.
editorial: Candidate strings are the borders of s; they form the chain b1 > b2 > ... where b1 = pi[n-1] and b_{k+1} = pi[b_k - 1].

A border of length L has an inner occurrence if and only if some position j ≤ n-2 has pi[j] ≥ L. If pi[j] ≥ L, the prefix of length pi[j] ends at j and starts at j - pi[j] + 1 ≥ 1, and its first L characters are a copy of s[0..L-1] that starts at the same index and ends no later than j ≤ n-2, so the copy is strictly inside. Conversely an inner occurrence ending at j forces pi[j] ≥ L.
Therefore compute M = max(pi[0..n-2]) and take the first border in the chain with length at most M. Everything is O(n).
